ch38.note: Lü Zhengcao (吕正操, 1904–2009), a former Northeastern (Manchurian) Army officer who went over to the Communists and built and led their guerrilla forces in central Hebei; it was his command that absorbed the defector Zhu Zhankui.

An administrative inspector-commissioner (专员, zhuanyuan) headed a 'special district' grouping a dozen or more counties—an intermediate tier of government the Nationalists set between the province and the county, with police and militia at its command.

The Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, spanning parts of Shaanxi, Gansu, and Ningxia, was the central Communist base area of the war years, with Yan'an—the Party's headquarters from the mid-1930s until 1947—as its seat.

Ren Zhuoxuan (任卓宣, pen name Ye Qing, 1896–1990), an early Communist who broke with the Party and became a prominent Nationalist anti-Communist theorist; the 'Mr. Xu Foguan' named beside him was Xu Fuguan (徐复观), a well-known New Confucian scholar and former army officer.
The Ming Xiaoling, the great tomb of the founding Ming emperor Zhu Yuanzhang, set on the wooded slopes east of Nanjing—here a night-march muster point.

The 'Selected Grade' (简任, jianren) was the senior tier of the Nationalist civil service, ranking just below the specially-appointed (ministerial) grade—so the title fixes just how high a civil rank the man held.
